messages:
maya_finance: quick heads-up 1: Orbital's November invoice shows ~100% extra embed units concentrated in the 00:00-01:00 UTC slot for the billing window. looks like exact duplicates rather than spikes. can ops confirm? :mag:
liam_platform: do you have an example request id or a small sample? that helps to check dedupe keys in the ledger ingest pipeline.;
tori_billing: pulled a shallow diff from the export:
```
2026-11-05T00:12:03Z req=rz9k orbital embed_count=12
2026-11-05T00:12:03Z req=rz9k orbital embed_count=12  <-- duplicate row
```

eli_sre: interesting. batch aggregator (meter-aggregator v3) had a config change last week to support local-day reporting. i remember the deploy note mentioned timezone handling. i'll check the canary logs.;
batch-bot: LOG: meter-aggregator-v3[worker-2] 2026-11-05T00:00:01Z INFO aggregating window start=2026-11-05T00:00:00 tz=America/Los_Angeles policy=rollover-mode:local;
liam_platform: that tz looks wrong. we expect all aggregation windows to be anchored to UTC. if the aggregator ran twice (once UTC, once local) for the same absolute times, that could duplicate rows into the ledger if dedupe key was window_based rather than request_id-based.;
maya_finance: rough numbers from invoice: duplicate embed units = ~125,400 across 00:00-01:00 UTC for orbital (invoice line 3). other customers have smaller bumps.
tori_billing: quick query to find candidate duplicates we ran: 
```
SELECT request_id, customer_id, COUNT(*) as c, SUM(embed_count) as sum_emb
FROM billing_raw
WHERE recorded_at >= '2026-11-05T00:00:00Z' AND recorded_at < '2026-11-05T01:00:00Z'
GROUP BY request_id, customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY c DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
we found ~18k request_ids duplicated in that window.

eli_sre: root cause hypothesis: env var METER_AGG_TZ was unset during the v3 rollout, aggregator fell back to container local tz (infra hosts in us-west-2 -> America/Los_Angeles) while other parts of the pipeline still used UTC. dedupe key is (customer, window_start, request_hash). with two window_start values mapping the same requests to distinct rows, the ledger accepted both rows.
liam_platform: mitigation options: (A) run a targeted dedupe job that collapses duplicates by request_hash for that window and produce a delta CSV for finance (safer, auditable but touches ledger joins), (B) issue a manual invoice credit for affected customers and then run a verification-only dedupe to ensure no other windows were impacted.
maya_finance: finance prefers ledger fixes for audit trail, but need to understand blast radius and complexity. what's ETA for a safe dedupe?
tori_billing: estimate: produce candidate delta CSV (request_id, customer_id, original_rows, deduped_embed_sum, trace_id) ~ ~18k rows -> compressed 1.1MB. verification run to reconcile with invoice exports ~ 90m. actual ledger-adjust apply (replay) including downstream cache invalidation ~3-4 hours with on-call oversight. will need head-of-billing sign-off for ledger writes.;
eli_sre: i'll create a dry-run dedupe workflow: run dedupe against a snapshot (no writes) and produce checksums: pre_checksum/post_checksum and sample rows. if checksums match expected invoice drops, we can schedule the write during low-traffic window. i'll post the script: 
```
# sample dedupe sketch
pg_dump -t billing_raw --data-only --where "recorded_at >= '2026-11-05T00:00:00Z' AND recorded_at < '2026-11-05T01:00:00Z'" > snapshot.sql
python dedupe.py --snapshot snapshot.sql --key request_hash --out delta.csv --mode dryrun
```

batch-bot: NOTE: snapshot size estimate = ~42MB compressed, candidate delta rows = 18,120, estimated embed unit delta = 125,400.;
liam_platform: i will also flip METER_AGG_TZ to UTC in the canary env and run a 1-hour backtest to ensure no other windows produce duplicate keys.;
maya_finance: ok. please @mention me when the delta CSV is ready. finance will review and likely request ledger apply for auditability, pending head-of-billing approval. we'll also need a short note for the customer explaining root cause and remediation (billing adjustment).
tori_billing: drafting customer note: "We identified duplicate meter rows during a nightly aggregation window caused by a timezone misconfiguration in our aggregation service. We've prepared an audited ledger adjustment to correct the invoice and will apply it after validation. No action required on your side." will circulate for legal review.;
eli_sre: action items: 1) fix METER_AGG_TZ in prod manifests (liam), 2) run dry-run dedupe and produce delta CSV (eli), 3) finance review + head-of-billing sign-off (maya/tori), 4) apply ledger fix in maintenance window and notify customers (all). ETA: dry-run + CSV ~90m, patch config + canary test ~30m, ledger apply after approval ~3-4h.
maya_finance: thanks. marking as provisional ledger-adjust request. will open formal ticket for head-of-billing approval with the CSV once ready. :white_check_mark:
